hints: Start by remembering what the Contact process is really for, and what Z must be in aqueous solution.
An aqueous solution of Z is strongly acidic, so think about what type of gas (acidic or basic) would neutralise it.
Check each listed process for the one that makes a familiar alkaline gas that forms a salt with acids.
walkthrough:
**Identify Z from the Contact process**

The Contact process oxidises sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide, which is then converted to sulfuric acid. So Z is $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$

**Decide what gas is needed**

An aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a strong acid. To neutralise it we need a basic (alkaline) gas.

The common basic gas you must know is ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$:
$$2\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$$

**Match the gas to the process**

The Haber process combines nitrogen and hydrogen to make ammonia gas.

$$\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$$
This is the only option that produces a basic gas, so it neutralises Z.

options.A: Lightning provides enough energy for $\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$, which is further oxidised to $\text{NO}_2$. These nitrogen oxides dissolve to give acidic solutions, so they would add acidity to Z, not neutralise it.
options.B: High temperature combustion in engines also forms $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$, plus $\text{CO}_2$ from the fuel. All of these are acidic gases, so they cannot neutralise sulfuric acid.
options.C: The Haber process makes ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, which is basic. It reacts with and neutralises aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form ammonium sulfate.
options.D: Group 2 nitrates decompose on heating, e.g. $2\text{Mg}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. The gaseous products $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are acidic or neutral, not basic, so they cannot neutralise Z.
